name: MPT Sheesh Mahal Restaurant
area: Inside Sheesh Mahal heritage hotel, Orchha Fort complex
signature_dish: Royal-style Bundeli dinner under fort arches
why_it_matters: MPT Sheesh Mahal is the only restaurant in India that operates inside an active 1763 royal palace — built by Udait Singh as a Bundela royal guesthouse and now run by Madhya Pradesh Tourism as a heritage hotel. The 'Palace of Mirrors' gets its name from the glazed blue-green tiles (not actual mirrors). Dining is under high arches and chandeliers; the menu surfaces local Bundeli dishes like murg bundelkhand and kothi-ghat fish curry that you can't find at the village stalls below.
insider_tip: Reserve the courtyard table — palace interior is good, the open arches with the Jahangir Mahal view at dusk is the whole point. Walk-in possible off-season (Apr-Jun, Aug-Sep) but Oct-Mar weekends are full. Open to non-hotel guests but bookings are essential during Diwali-New Year and February weddings.
signature_address: MPT Sheesh Mahal, Jahangir Mahal Road, Orchha Fort, Orchha, Madhya Pradesh 472246

name: Bundelkhand Riverside — The Turquoise Diner
area: Bundelkhand Riverside Heritage Hotel, Betwa banks
signature_dish: Bundeli mutton with kothi-ghat fish curry on a riverside terrace
why_it_matters: The Turquoise Diner is the in-house restaurant of Bundelkhand Riverside Heritage Hotel — set on 55 acres along the Betwa River. Inspired by the blue-tiled Jahangir Mahal, the dining room repeats the turquoise-tile motif. The menu pushes Bundelkhand-specific dishes (murg bundelkhand, kothi-ghat fish curry — a fish dish named after Orchha's bathing ghat) more deliberately than most local kitchens.
insider_tip: Evening drinks with a singer 7:30-9pm is a lower-cost way to use the property — order one drink and a starter rather than a full dinner if budget is tight. Sunset on the riverside terrace 5:30-6:30pm (Oct-Feb) is the photo. Walk-in possible but reservations preferred Nov-Feb weekends.
signature_address: Bundelkhand Riverside, Betwa Banks, Orchha, Madhya Pradesh 472246

name: Ramraja Restaurant & Cafe
area: Near Ram Raja Temple, Main Bazaar
signature_dish: Pure-veg thali after Ram Raja darshan
why_it_matters: Family-run pure-veg restaurant near the Ram Raja Temple, opened in 1994 — 31 years old. Lonely Planet-recommended, the default lunch stop after Ram Raja morning aarti for families on the Bundelkhand pilgrim circuit. Butter paneer masala and dal-fry are the orders the kitchen has been making the same way for two decades.
insider_tip: Crowded 12:30-2:30pm after late-morning aarti; arrive at 12 sharp or after 2:30 for an open table. Cash and UPI both. Skip non-veg expectations — this is a pure-veg pilgrim-side kitchen by design.
signature_address: Near Ram Raja Temple, Main Bazaar, Orchha, Madhya Pradesh 472246

name: Apoorva Betwa Tarang
signature_dish: Pure-veg thali with Raj Mahal rooftop view
why_it_matters: AC dining-room budget restaurant on Betwa Riverside with a rooftop terrace that has stupendous views of Raj Mahal — Lonely Planet's pick as the best veg-budget restaurant in Orchha. Thalis run ₹130-₹350. The same family also runs Laxmi Betwa Tarang next door (similar format); the Apoorva branch has more reviews and a slightly cleaner kitchen.
insider_tip: Eat on the rooftop, not the AC room — the Raj Mahal silhouette at sunset (Oct-Mar 6pm) is the view. Skip in May-June if the rooftop is the plan — it's too hot until after 7pm. Best thali under ₹350 in Orchha.
signature_address: Main Bazaar / Betwa Riverside, Orchha, Madhya Pradesh 472246
